from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Dimensional Ladder", [
            "A 2D circle is defined by points equidistant from center.",
            "Distance formula generalizes this to 3D spheres.",
            "Equation x² + y² + z² = r² defines a 3D ball."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        point = Dot(color=WHITE)
        line = Line(LEFT*0.5, RIGHT*0.5, color=WHITE)
        circle = Circle(radius=0.5, color=WHITE)
        sphere = Sphere(radius=0.5, color=WHITE)
        
        labels = VGroup(
            Text("0D", font_size=18),
            Text("1D", font_size=18),
            Text("2D", font_size=18),
            Text("3D", font_size=18)
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.play(Create(point), Write(self.place_at_grid(labels[0], 'A1')))
        self.play(Create(line), Write(self.place_at_grid(labels[1], 'A3')))
        self.play(Create(circle), Write(self.place_at_grid(labels[2], 'A5')))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.play(Create(sphere), Write(self.place_at_grid(labels[3], 'C3')))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700")
        equation = MathTex("x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = r^2", color="#FFD700")
        self.place_in_area(equation, 'D3', 'E5')
        self.play(Write(equation))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Does a high-dimensional sphere hold more volume?",
            "Volume approaches zero as dimensions increase.",
            "Most volume concentrates near the sphere's crust.",
            "Analogy: In high dimensions, the core is empty.",
            "Think of it as an 'Orange of Doom'."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Counter-Intuitive Volume Paradox", lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup visual elements
        sphere = Circle(radius=1.5, color=WHITE)
        vol_label = Text("V(n) -> 0", font_size=24)
        comparison = VGroup(Circle(radius=1.2), Circle(radius=0.4)).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)
        crust_highlight = Annulus(inner_radius=1.2, outer_radius=1.5, color=RED)
        orange = Circle(radius=1.5, color=ORANGE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.place_at_grid(sphere, 'B3')
        self.play(Create(sphere), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.place_at_grid(vol_label, 'E3')
        self.play(FadeIn(vol_label), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.place_at_grid(comparison, 'C3')
        self.play(FadeIn(comparison), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.place_at_grid(crust_highlight, 'B3')
        self.play(Create(crust_highlight), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#00FFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.place_at_grid(orange, 'B3')
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(sphere, orange), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FF4500")
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "How do we visualize high-dimensional objects?",
            "We project them into 2D and 3D cross-sections.",
            "A 4D sphere slice appears as a growing circle."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the Invisible: The Slice Method", lecture_lines)
        
        # Mobjects
        sphere = Sphere(radius=1.0, color=BLUE).set_opacity(0.3)
        plane = Square(side_length=2.5, color=WHITE).set_opacity(0.1)
        slice_circle = Circle(radius=0.5, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.8)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[0]))
        self.place_in_area(sphere, 'B2', 'D4', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(sphere), run_time=1.5)
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[1]))
        self.place_at_grid(plane, 'C3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(plane), run_time=1.0)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[2]))
        self.place_at_grid(slice_circle, 'C3', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # Animating the circle growing
        self.play(
            GrowFromCenter(slice_circle),
            run_time=2.0
        )
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Real-World Application: Machine Learning", [
            "High-dimensional spheres are practical tools in AI.",
            "Support Vector Machines use them for classification.",
            "They effectively separate complex data clusters."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show high-dimensional feature space. Color #FFFFFF.
        feature_space = VGroup(*[
            Dot(color=WHITE, radius=0.05).move_to(np.random.uniform(-1.5, 1.5, 3))
            for _ in range(50)
        ])
        self.place_in_area(feature_space, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(feature_space))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Represent data points as spheres. Color #FFFFFF.
        data_points = VGroup(*[
            Sphere(radius=0.1, color=WHITE).move_to(np.random.uniform(-1, 1, 3))
            for _ in range(10)
        ])
        self.place_in_area(data_points, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(data_points))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Demonstrate volume concentration effect. Color #FFD700.
        hyperplane = Square(side_length=2, color="#FFD700").set_fill(opacity=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(hyperplane, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(Create(hyperplane))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700")
        
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Unveiling the High-Dimensional Sphere: Geometry in N-Dimensions

sections.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: The Dimensional Ladder (0:00-0:45)
sections.content: Briefly recap the definition of a sphere in 2D (circle) and 3D (ball). Introduce the distance formula (Pythagorean theorem generalized) as the foundation for defining a set of points equidistant from a center.
sections.example: Visual transition: A point expands into a line, then a circle, then a sphere, emphasizing the equation x² + y² + z² = r².

sections.title: Defining the N-Sphere (0:45-1:45)
sections.content: Mathematically define an n-sphere as the set of points at distance r from the origin in n-dimensional space. Visualize this by adding a 4th coordinate (w), where x² + y² + z² + w² = r².
sections.example: A 'Hyper-cube' containing a 'Hyper-sphere'. Imagine a 4D robot scanning a room; it sees a 3D slice of the 4D sphere.

sections.title: The Counter-Intuitive Volume Paradox (1:45-3:15)
sections.content: Challenge the audience: Does a high-dimensional sphere hold more volume? Explain that as dimension n increases, the volume of a sphere of fixed radius actually approaches zero. Highlight the concentration of volume near the 'crust'.
sections.example: Analogy: An 'Orange of Doom'. In 100 dimensions, almost all the volume of the orange is in the peel, while the 'fruit' (the core) is effectively empty space.

sections.title: Visualizing the Invisible: The Slice Method (3:15-4:15)
sections.content: Explain how we interpret high-dimensional objects using 2D and 3D cross-sections. This is how physicists and data scientists 'view' high-dimensional data clusters.
sections.example: Animated 3D projection: A sphere passing through a 2D plane appears as a growing and shrinking circle—analogous to a 4D sphere passing through our 3D world.

sections.title: Real-World Application: Machine Learning (4:15-5:00)
sections.content: Conclusion: High-dimensional spheres are not just theoretical; they are the basis for 'Support Vector Machines' in AI, helping classify data in high-dimensional space.
sections.example: A classification algorithm acting like a 'Hyper-sphere' filter that separates images of 'cats' from 'dogs' based on thousands of pixel-based variables.
